known_risks.risk: DiscussionsView has two render paths (standalone + card). Removing MUI imports that appear unused in one path will break the other. Always check both paths before removing imports.

known_risks.risk: History is append-only and stores a SNAPSHOT of the runbook name at completion time â€” renaming or deleting a runbook must NOT rewrite or remove past history lines
known_risks.mitigation: recordRun copies runbook.name into the RunbookRun object; history array is only ever prepended to, never filtered by runbookId

known_risks.risk: top-three and weekly are locked at the top of col 1 (not in the moveable layout) to preserve their single-mount event-bus subscriptions across view-mode changes.

known_risks.mitigation: loadLayout() in useModuleLayout appends missing modules to col3; ALL_MODULES constant is the authoritative list.

known_risks.risk: getISOWeekDates in GCalProvider uses local date arithmetic but must not use toISOString().substring(0,10) to format the result â€” toISOString converts to UTC, so midnight local time in a timezone ahead of UTC (e.g. Paris UTC+2) becomes the previous day in UTC, shifting the whole week array one day early and causing syncGCalRef to target the wrong ISO week.
known_risks.mitigation: Build date strings from getFullYear()/getMonth()/getDate() (local calendar components). See toLocalDateStr() in GCalProvider.tsx. Applies the KR-006 rule to all date-string builders, not only day arithmetic.

known_risks.risk: shellView ('dashboard'|'fullscreen') and activeModule are the single source of truth for the shell view; they must persist to window.localStorage (shell:view / shell:active) and NOT be cloud-synced â€” same pattern as layout:modules and the split boundaries. A stale activeModule (module hidden/removed since last session) must not render an empty body.
known_risks.mitigation: Read/write shell:view + shell:active via window.localStorage directly (not PersistenceService); guard activeModule against unknown ids by falling back to firstAvailableModule(); keep StatusBar mounted above the strip so it never unmounts on a view switch.

known_risks.risk: viewMode 'day'|'week' is renamed to shellView 'dashboard'|'fullscreen' across App.tsx. This is DISTINCT from WeeklyView's own internal day/week grid toggle, which must not be folded into the shell switch â€” conflating them breaks the planner's grid control.
known_risks.mitigation: Rename the shell-level state only; leave WeeklyView's day/week prop + toggle intact; update every viewMode reference and its tests; map dashboardâ†”(old 'day') and fullscreenâ†”(old 'week' + activeModule).

known_risks.risk: The strip is a third view type per module and its height is CONSTANT â€” each chip is a single ellipsis-truncated line. The early variant that stacked three lines grew the strip and was rejected; stacking lines or letting the strip grow is a regression.
known_risks.mitigation: StripChip renders exactly one truncated line; the counter carries quantity; below the md breakpoint the strip scrolls horizontally (states.md Â§6) instead of growing or wrapping.

known_risks.risk: Alert chips tint the tile via color-mix(in oklch, var(--warn|--bad) X%, transparent). If --bad or --warn is undefined the color-mix is invalid â†’ the tile renders transparent and flag text falls back to --ink, silently losing the alert colour (observed when a cloned token head omitted --bad; the 'MES date passed' alert lost its red).
known_risks.mitigation: Ensure --good/--warn/--bad/--info are defined in BOTH theme blocks of tokens.ts/theme.ts; one alert tone per chip; the empty state takes precedence over alert.

known_risks.risk: Each module's useXxxStripChip() selector runs on every render of the always-mounted strip; a heavy or non-defensive selector (raw cast of persisted data) can thrash or crash the strip.
known_risks.mitigation: Selectors merge persisted values with defaults field-by-field (parseData pattern), are memoised, and read through usePersistence() (KR-037) â€” never a raw cast, never useContext(PersistenceContext).

known_risks.risk: Which modules appear in the strip and their order persist under strip:chips (useModuleLayout pattern); a code change that adds a module must not silently drop ids missing from a stored order.
known_risks.mitigation: Append unknown ids per an authoritative ALL_STRIP_CHIPS constant (mirrors KR-056); persist via window.localStorage, not cloud-synced.

known_risks.risk: MES/MEP becomes a moveable dashboard module; adding 'mes-and-mep' to ModuleId requires DEFAULT_LAYOUT and the renderSecondaryModule switch to cover it, or the module is silently dropped (KR-056 family). Existing persisted layout:modules must stay valid.
known_risks.mitigation: Extend ModuleId + DEFAULT_LAYOUT + the renderSecondaryModule switch together; rely on the missing-id â†’ col3 migration; keep top-three and weekly pinned at the top of col 1.

known_risks.risk: activeModule supersedes weekSidePanel as the fullscreen target; every setWeekSidePanel call site and the one-one:open subscription must migrate. Per-module Fullscreen components must be keyed by id so React remounts on switch (BUG-001/005), or one module's scroll/state leaks into the next; single-mount modules (top-three, weekly) must stay mounted to preserve their event-bus subscriptions.
known_risks.mitigation: Introduce activeModule (persisted shell:active); render a FullscreenHost switch keyed by id; migrate all weekSidePanel references; firstAvailableModule() skips modules with no Fullscreen view.

known_risks.risk: StatusBar is a dumb renderer â€” it must never import module-specific hooks or components directly. All right-of-spacer content comes through statusBarSlots: ReactNode[] injected by App.tsx. New modules add a statusBarSlot component to their ModuleShellContribution and register in MODULE_CONTRIBUTIONS.
known_risks.mitigation: Keep StatusBar props to: shellView, onToggleView, onOpenPreferences, statusBarSlots. Any module wanting a StatusBar presence exports a zero-prop ComponentType via ModuleShellContribution.statusBarSlot; App.tsx instantiates it.

known_risks.risk: ModuleShellContribution is the single contract for all shell surface contributions (statusBarSlot, stripChip, dashboardCard, fullscreenView, parametersSection). Adding a surface or a module contribution must go through this type in brain/types/shellContribution.ts and be registered in MODULE_CONTRIBUTIONS in App.tsx.
known_risks.mitigation: brain/types/shellContribution.ts is the source of truth. App.tsx assembles contributions per surface using useMemo([], []) â€” zero re-renders on mount since MODULE_CONTRIBUTIONS is a module-level constant.

known_risks.risk: Notes strip chip requires a notes:general:updated-at persistence key. useGeneralNote.saveNote must persist this ISO timestamp alongside the note text. Without it the Notes chip cannot show modifie hh:mm.
known_risks.mitigation: Add persistence.set(notes:general:updated-at, new Date().toISOString()) inside useGeneralNote.saveNote (before the debounce flush). Read notes:general:updated-at directly in useNotesStripChip via usePersistence().

known_risks.risk: Runbooks interrupted-run alert must scan runbooks:progress:* keys via persistence.keys(runbooks:progress:) and check Object.values(parsed.checked).some(v => v). Do NOT use runbooks:active as the interrupted-run indicator â€” it is a last-opened marker, not a progress indicator.
known_risks.mitigation: In useRunbooksStripChip: persistence.keys(runbooks:progress:).filter(k => { const p = persistence.get(k); return p && Object.values(p.checked ?? {}).some(v => v) }). If any such key exists, return alert state.

known_risks.risk: One-one staleness threshold must be a named constant DEFAULT_STALE_WEEKS = 2. The selector picks the person with the OLDEST last-seen date; a person with NO entries uses their createdAt as the reference date. The threshold is not defined in the design, so 2 weeks is the default.

known_risks.risk: The muted prop on Chip in chips.jsx is a GALLERY-ONLY visualization aid (0.4 opacity, shows no-alert row grayed out). In the real strip, modules with no alert (Notes, Pensine) render their plain normal chip. Do NOT implement muted as a StripChip prop or state.
known_risks.mitigation: StripChip.tsx has no muted prop. Chip selectors for Notes/Pensine return { state: normal, ... } when no alert applies â€” the component renders identically to a normal chip.

known_risks.risk: Strip chip height is driven by the parent grid container (height: 60px), not by the chip. Each chip must use height: 100% and min-width: 0 to fill its grid cell. Setting a fixed height on StripChip breaks the equal-cell layout.
known_risks.mitigation: Strip grid: height: 60px; grid-auto-columns: 1fr. StripChip sx: { height: 100%, minWidth: 0 }. Do NOT set a pixel height on StripChip.

Reference compliant implementations: RunbookRunner.tsx (dialog variant) + OneOnOneDetail.tsx.

known_risks.risk: ITER-14: GCalEventDialog must be keyed by event id (Dialog key={event.id}) so React remounts when the user clicks a different event without closing the popup first â€” prevents stale description HTML from a previous event leaking through (BUG-001/005 pattern).
known_risks.mitigation: Always set key={entry.id} (or key={event.htmlLink}) on GCalEventDialog; never share a single Dialog instance across events via open/close state alone.

known_risks.risk: WeeklyView variant semantics are load-bearing: variant=dashboard must render DayView (single day + nav arrows); variant=fullscreen must render WeekView (5-day calendar grid). Swapping them is a silent regression â€” the wrong view renders without a compile or test error. A visual-refresh patch may inadvertently reset this.
known_risks.mitigation: After any patch touching WeeklyView.tsx: verify dashboard column 1 shows DayView (prev/next arrows visible) and fullscreen weekly shows WeekView (PrÃ©cÃ©dente/Suivante week nav visible). The variant prop comment in WeeklyView is the authoritative contract.

known_risks.risk: Every dashboard module widget must wrap its content in <Box sx={{ px: {xs:1,sm:2}, py:4 }}><Card><CardContent>. Omitting the Card wrapper makes the module appear visually detached from the rest of the dashboard (no shadow, no surface elevation, no border-radius).
known_risks.mitigation: When restoring, moving, or creating a dashboard widget: always apply the canonical shell Box > Card > CardContent. py:4 is the standard vertical gap; px follows the xs:1/sm:2 responsive pattern.

known_risks.risk: The key-by-entity-id rule (BUG-001/005) applies to fullscreen split-panel panes, not only MUI Dialogs. Any stateful pane or form that displays/edits a selected entity from a list must carry key={entity.id} so React remounts on selection change â€” without it, useState retains the previous entity's local state (text, images, tags) and the UI shows stale data.
known_risks.mitigation: Whenever a component receives a selected entity as a prop and initialises local state from it (useState(entity.body)), key it by entity.id at the call site. Applies to: Dialogs, SidePanels, column 2/3 panes in split layouts, drawers.

known_risks.risk: DaySpine SPINE_START/SPINE_END and TaskItem TimePicker minTime/maxTime must always match. Visual-refresh patches that touch DaySpine tend to reset SPINE_START/SPINE_END to a wider window (e.g. 8-20) while the pickers stay at the narrower range (9-19), creating a mismatch where times outside the picker range appear on the spine but cannot be created.
known_risks.mitigation: After any patch touching DaySpine.tsx: verify SPINE_START == picker minTime hour and SPINE_END == picker maxTime hour. The canonical range is 09h-19h (matching working-hours convention and picker constraints).

known_risks.risk: DayView and WeekView must stay in parity for WeeklyContributionEntry rendering. When a new rendering field (chipLabel, displayVariant, tone, tag...) is added to WeekView, the same branch must be added to DayView â€” and vice versa. chipToneSx lives in weekUtils.ts and is the single source of tone-colour logic for both views. DayView chipLabel rows use chip + title text (px:1 py:0.5 borderRadius:1, hover bgcolor) to match the plain-text row layout.
known_risks.mitigation: After any change to WeeklyContributionEntry rendering in WeekView or DayView: open the other view and verify the same rendering cases are handled. chipToneSx import is the signal â€” if one view imports it, the other should too.

known_risks.risk: Inline link XSS guard: when rendering [label](url) patterns in task rows, only create <a> elements for http:// and https:// URLs. Store any other protocol as-is in task.text but never inject it into an href. Always add rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" to rendered anchors. Use parseMarkdownLinks() from todoUtils â€” never roll a separate link renderer.

Paste detection for inline link insertion: the onPaste handler in AddBar and TaskRow inline edit must check BOTH (a) clipboard text starts with http:// or https:// AND (b) the input has a non-empty selection before calling e.preventDefault() and splicing the [label](url) markdown. If either condition is false, fall through to default paste.

Plain-text contexts must strip [label](url) to just "label": strip chip content (useTodoStripChip), calendar entry titles (TodoContributionSlot), and any aria-label that includes task text. Use stripMarkdownLinks() from todoUtils as the single normaliser â€” never expose raw markdown syntax in read-only or accessible text contexts.

TaskRichInput lazy-mount (Option A): the Tiptap editor mounts only when a row enters edit mode and unmounts on save/cancel. useEditor returns null on the first render â€” EditorContent renders an empty div until ProseMirror initialises. The add-bar wrapper Box must have enough padding/min-height to remain clickable during that brief null state.

tiptap-markdown is serialisation/deserialisation only â€” it does NOT provide live markdown shortcut typing. Typing **text** does NOT auto-convert to bold in the editor. Formatting requires Ctrl+B (StarterKit input rule) or the BubbleMenu. Do not add a Markdown shortcut layer unless explicitly requested.

stripTaskMarkdown must be applied wherever task.text or subtask.text reaches external systems: eventBus emissions (projects:add-to-top-three, projects:add-to-day), calendar contribution entry titles in ProjectsContributionSlot, HillChart SVG <title> elements and legend text labels, and any aria-label containing task text.

renderTaskRichText XSS guard: only http/https URLs become anchor elements â€” other protocols are rendered as plain text. Anchor onClick calls e.stopPropagation() so clicks do not bubble to the parent Typography onClick handler (which starts inline editing). Never create an anchor with an unvalidated href from task.text.

TaskRichInput is a shared brain component (brain/components/TaskRichInput.tsx). Features must import it from brain/, never from each other. When a new feature needs inline rich text, import from brain/components/TaskRichInput â€” do not recreate it locally.

parseMarkdownLinks and stripMarkdownLinks in todoUtils.ts now handle bold (**), italic (*), strikethrough (~~), AND links ([label](url)). If called in a context that previously only expected link stripping (e.g. strip chip, calendar titles), the extended stripping is now automatic â€” no separate call needed. The regex priority order matters: bold (**text**) must match before italic (*text*) to prevent partial ** matches.

TaskRichInput forwardRef test mocks must expose focus() via useImperativeHandle â€” not just forward the ref to the DOM input. Without it, TodoPanel's focusInput() (called from empty-state CTA) silently does nothing and the CTA focus test fails. Pattern: useImperativeHandle(ref, () => ({ focus: () => inputRef.current?.focus() })).

Soft/line token variants (--good/warn/bad-soft/line) affect all chipToneSx() call sites across DayView and WeekView. A missing token causes color-mix() to render transparent (KR-061 family). Always add to BOTH light and dark palette blocks in tokens.ts and expose in theme.ts :root. Verify light and dark after adding.

DiscussionModal read mode initialises formState from the discussion prop via useEffect on open+id+mode. Read mode must render from the live discussion prop (not formState) to avoid showing stale data when the modal opens directly in read mode after an edit. The existing pattern already does this â€” do not refactor it to formState-only.
known_risks.mitigation: Keep the read mode JSX branch reading from discussion (not formState) for all fields; only the create/edit branch uses formState.

known_risks.risk: KR-VR3: the subtasks->note migration runs once at read time in the useProjects initializer; it must preserve any pre-existing task.note (note text first, then the converted task list) and only strip subtasks after conversion. Persist the migrated shape on the next write so it is idempotent.
known_risks.mitigation: Migration runs in the useState initializer â€” never in a useEffect or on every render. Append the GFM task list to any existing note text before dropping the subtasks field. Write back immediately after migration so subsequent loads skip it.

known_risks.risk: tiptap-markdown serialises task items as GFM '- [ ]' / '- [x]'; countNoteTasks must match the same markers it emits (leading '-' or '*' then '[ ]' or '[x]', case-insensitive). TaskItem requires TaskList; configure TaskList with nested: true so checklists can sit inside bullet lists.
known_risks.mitigation: countNoteTasks regex: /^[\-\*]\s+\[([ xX])\]/m â€” matches both '-' and '*', case-insensitive x. Tiptap config: TaskList.configure({ nested: true }) + TaskItem.configure({ nested: true }).

known_risks.risk: Note typing is per-keystroke â€” debounce writes 500ms + pendingRef + unmount-flush (KR-012); never write on every onChange.
known_risks.mitigation: Use the same debounce pattern as discussions (KR-012): debounceRef + pendingRef + useEffect cleanup that flushes on unmount.

known_risks.risk: Removing ProjectSubtask is a breaking type change: delete addSubtask/updateSubtask/deleteSubtask from useProjects and the matching ProjectDialog props, and update ProjectsView.test.tsx / useProjects.test.tsx (drop subtask tests; add migration + countNoteTasks tests). Tests are updated by the build step, not by a patch.
known_risks.mitigation: Before removing any subtask surface: grep for addSubtask/updateSubtask/deleteSubtask/ProjectSubtask across the whole codebase and remove every reference atomically. Run tsc --noEmit to catch missed callsites.

known_risks.risk: DiaryContributor.getEntries must be pure and synchronous — async sources (e.g. gcal events) cannot participate in the diary; attempting to use async operations inside getEntries will produce empty or stale results.
known_risks.mitigation: Do not add async code inside getEntries. Async data must be pre-fetched and stored in a ref or state before registration.

known_risks.risk: Report generation must always be user-triggered — never auto-trigger generateReport on mount. Once the real Cloudflare AI service is wired, auto-generation on mount would silently cost money per page load.
known_risks.mitigation: Keep the Generer button as the sole trigger. Never call generateReport in a useEffect without explicit user action.

known_risks.risk: Todo tasks completed before version 0.22.0 have no completedAt field and will not appear in diary reports for past dates.
known_risks.mitigation: Acceptable as documented. No migration needed. Reports from 0.22.0 onward will capture completedAt correctly.

known_risks.risk: flushSync inside an async function in React 18 concurrent mode causes the synchronous re-render to build a new fiber tree; subsequent async state updates target the old fiber and consumers do not re-render (display never updates).
known_risks.mitigation: Never use flushSync to show a spinner before an async call. Instead, keep isGenerating as local component state; React 18 naturally flushes setIsGenerating(true) at the await boundary so the spinner renders before the async work runs.

known_risks.risk: DiaryContributionSlot today-fallback: todo, project-manager, and discussions slots use localDayStr() (today) when the primary date field (completedAt, dueDate, note.date) is absent, so legacy undated done items surface in the first generated report.
known_risks.mitigation: Intentional and temporary. Remove the fallback once all data carries proper dates. Do not extend this pattern to new modules — new modules must set a date at creation time.

known_risks.risk: Cloudflare Workers Request.json() does not accept generic type parameters in the Workers runtime — the TypeScript overload exists but the generic is stripped at runtime and may break in strict CF type environments.
known_risks.mitigation: Always use (await request.json()) as T — type-assert after the call, never pass a type argument to .json<T>().

known_risks.risk: AI fetch calls (CloudflareReportService) have no built-in timeout — a slow or hung Workers AI response leaves the spinner running indefinitely and blocks the user.
known_risks.mitigation: Always wrap AI fetch calls in an AbortController with a 45s timeout. Map AbortError to a user-friendly French message. Clear the timeout in a finally block to avoid timer leaks.

known_risks.risk: Service instances (ReportService and similar factory-created singletons) created inline in JSX props produce a new object reference on every render, which can cause unnecessary downstream effects if the service is ever added to a hook dependency array.
known_risks.mitigation: Create service instances at module level when the factory depends only on module-level constants (e.g. WORKER_URL). Use useMemo only when the inputs are reactive (e.g. from state or props).

known_risks.risk: ContributionSlot components that call useNotesSelectionContext() (or any brain context hook) MUST be mounted INSIDE the matching provider in App.tsx. If placed outside the provider tree the hook returns the noop default silently — registerAction() does nothing, no error is thrown, and the action simply never appears in the BubbleMenu. Correct placement: nest the slot at the same depth as TodoContributionSlot, inside NotesProvider (and its children), not as a sibling of NotesProvider or above it. Diagnosis hint: if a registered BubbleMenu action vanishes, check App.tsx nesting before touching the slot component itself.

AI triage actions (task/pensine) are non-destructive: they create items in the target module but do NOT modify the source note. This is intentional — modifying the note based on AI output would be a destructive irreversible action. If future iterations want to remove accepted text from the note, that must be guarded by a ConfirmDialog. The pensine:note:create event bridges notes to PensineContributionSlot — PensineContributionSlot must remain always-mounted (inside NotesProvider, per KR-104) for this event to be consumed.

AI proposals are appended (non-destructive) to the decisions field as bullet points — they never replace existing content. confirm() returns the new decisions string; the caller must call handleSimpleField("decisions", next) to persist via the debounced update path (KR-012). Do not pass the updated string directly to onUpdate() — go through handleSimpleField so local state and persistence stay in sync.

TopThreeContextProvider must wrap both the registration slots and the TopThreeContextPanel. Slots rendered outside the provider fall back to the noop context (registerEntries returns () => void) and silently register nothing — the panel shows empty even when todo/project data exists.
known_risks.mitigation: Mount TopThreeContextProvider high in App.tsx, above ProjectsDialogProvider. All slots (TodoTopThreeContextSlot, ProjectTopThreeContextSlot) are always-mounted inside the provider tree. Verify by checking App.tsx nesting depth — same diagnostic as KR-104.

known_risks.risk: TopThreeProjectLinksSlot reads persistence once at mount — project link changes (e.g. user links a top-three task to a project while the app is open) will not reactively update the reverse indicator in ProjectsView until the next full remount. This is acceptable for an infrequent config action but callers should be aware.
known_risks.mitigation: For live reactivity, the slot would need to subscribe to top-three external-update window events. Not implemented in iter-15; add if user feedback requires it.

known_risks.risk: Any presentational component consumed by more than one feature belongs in brain/components/, never in a feature folder. StripChip is the canonical example of this violation — 9 features imported from features/strip/ creating a cross-feature dependency web. When a component is needed by >1 feature, move it to brain/components/ and re-export from brain/components/index.ts.
known_risks.mitigation: Before adding a component to a feature, check whether other features already import it or will need it. If yes, put it in brain/components/ from the start.

known_risks.risk: Generic utility functions (date helpers, string normalizers) used by more than one feature must live in brain/utils/ — never in a feature's own utils/. Importing from a sibling feature's utils/ is a cross-feature violation that creates hidden coupling. datesInRange() in journalUtils is the canonical example: imported by top-three.
known_risks.mitigation: When adding a utility to a feature, check if it has no domain coupling to that feature. If it is generic, put it in brain/utils/ immediately. grep for the function name before moving to verify all consumers.

known_risks.risk: Non-cloud-synced UI preferences (last-selected item, chip order, active markers) must be accessed via UIPreferencesService (brain/services/UIPreferencesService.ts) — never via raw window.localStorage in feature files. Raw localStorage calls in features create untestable, unauditable storage with no typed contract. UIPreferencesService is intentionally NOT wired through PersistenceService/CloudPersistenceService.
known_risks.mitigation: Use useUIPreferences() hook from brain/ for all non-synced local UI state. When adding a new UI preference key, add it to UIPreferenceKey union in UIPreferencesService.ts first.

known_risks.risk: Component and hook files over 400 lines are a split signal and should be decomposed into focused subcomponents or hooks. Files over 800 lines are a merge blocker — do not merge a PR that introduces or leaves an 800-line component. ProjectDialog.tsx (1329 lines) and RunbookRunner.tsx (1208 lines) are the canonical violations.
known_risks.mitigation: Before merging: count lines in all modified or new component/hook files. Above 400: add a split iteration to the spec. Above 800: split before merging.

known_risks.risk: // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps is never acceptable — it masks stale-closure bugs where a hook reads values from an outer scope without declaring them as dependencies. The canonical violation is ProjectDialog.tsx line 253 (missing 'projects' dependency) which causes makeForm() to produce stale form state when projects update.
known_risks.mitigation: Always fix the root cause: add the missing dependency to the array and verify no extra renders (use a ref guard if necessary). If the effect genuinely should not re-run when a value changes, extract that value to a ref. Never suppress the lint warning.

known_risks.risk: Sensitive credentials stored in localStorage (PAT, OAuth tokens, API keys) are an XSS attack surface on a cloud-first PWA — any injected script can read them. For a personal-use single-tenant PWA with no backend this is an unavoidable architectural trade-off, but the risk must be acknowledged and localised. Scattered raw localStorage.getItem('mes-and-mep:pat') calls make the attack surface invisible.
known_risks.mitigation: Register all sensitive localStorage keys in brain/persistenceKeys.ts with a /* SENSITIVE */ comment. Annotate sensitive UIPreferenceKey values with /* SENSITIVE */ so they appear in a single auditable place. Consider sessionStorage for keys that do not need to survive tab close (reduces the persistence window for credentials).

known_risks.risk: Module surfaces (strip chip, dashboard card, fullscreen) that hand-roll their own empty, loading, or error states diverge visually from each other and require per-module maintenance. JournalFullscreen is the canonical example: it used a centred CircularProgress + Typography for generating state and a centred Box + Typography + Button for empty state instead of InlineBanner(loading) and EmptyState.
known_risks.mitigation: Every module surface must use EmptyState for no-data states and InlineBanner for error/loading/offline states. The kit owns the look; the module supplies the copy and the CTA. For AI-generation in-progress states, use InlineBanner(loading=true). Import from the brain/components barrel, not the file path.

known_risks.risk: Decorative animations (pxPulse next-up dot, pxFadeIn just-scheduled entry) play even when the OS prefers reduced motion, violating WCAG 2.3 Guideline 2.3 and causing discomfort for users with vestibular disorders.
known_risks.mitigation: style.css includes a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block that redefines pxFadeIn and pxPulse to be static (no motion) while keeping the indicator dot and highlight visible. Global focus ring handled by *:focus-visible + --focus-ring token (added in design-system iter-1 via theme.ts MuiCssBaseline). Keyboard module switching is handled natively by MUI ToggleButton (arrow-key navigation within groups).

known_risks.risk: Signal accent-as-text split: --accent is the YELLOW FILL (backgrounds, borders, dots, button bg, rail, markers). --accent-ink is the dark-gold text/icon color when an accent-coloured glyph sits on paper in light mode; in dark mode --accent-ink === the bright yellow (legible on near-black). --accent-fg is the dark ink ON a yellow fill (e.g. a check or label inside a yellow contained button). Never colour a text or icon element with --accent — use --accent-ink on paper, --accent-fg on yellow fill.
known_risks.mitigation: After dropping in the Signal tokens.ts/theme.ts: run the accent-as-text sweep (design-system iter 11) changing every color: var(--accent) on a text/icon element to var(--accent-ink). Verify in light mode — yellow text on white paper is the failure signal. colourSemantics.ts must return --accent-ink for accent-coloured text, not --accent.

known_risks.risk: Phosphor icon weight convention: duotone for module/section/feature glyphs; bold for inline UI (buttons, row actions, chips, nav); fill for status markers (focus star, in-progress dot, Sparkle AI affordance). Duotone secondary layer renders at ~0.30 opacity by default. Size with size={n}; color with color="var(--accent-ink)" (never --accent for a glyph on paper).
known_risks.mitigation: After the icon codemod (design-system iter 13): verify each call site has the correct weight prop. grep for weight= in src/ and confirm every lucide-react import is gone.

known_risks.risk: Space Grotesk has no optical-size axis (opsz). All fontVariationSettings with opsz references become no-ops or errors after the token swap. Leaving them produces console warnings and may break variable-font fallback chains.
known_risks.mitigation: After tokens.ts drop-in (design-system iter 10): run the Fraunces/opsz grep (iter 12) and remove every fontVariationSettings / opsz string from all feature files and style.css. grep -r "opsz" src must return nothing after iter 12.

known_risks.risk: InProgressContext noop defaults are required: item rows (TaskItem, project rows, discussion rows) call isInProgress(ref) without knowing whether InProgressProvider is mounted. Without noop defaults the hook throws outside its provider, blanking any surface that imports it. The same pattern as NotesBucketContext / DiscussionContext.
known_risks.mitigation: InProgressContext created with createContext({ isInProgress: () => false, setInProgress: () => {}, clear: () => {}, list: () => [] }). Walk-the-board depends on this — build en-cours first or stub InProgressContext before coding walk-the-board.

known_risks.risk: WalkItems must be deduped by ref: the same task can be surfaced by both Weekly (as a scheduled block) and Top 3 (as a priority). Showing it twice and routing the decision twice creates inconsistent state in two modules.
known_risks.mitigation: useWalk() deduplicates the collected WalkItem[] by ref key (surface+id) before sorting. Each surface contributor maps only its own canonical items; the dedup runs after collection, before display.

known_risks.risk: WalkOrderService must degrade: when the sync key is absent or the device is offline, the walk must still function using a deterministic comparator (overdue → blocking → today → quick). Never block the flow advance or card display on a pending model call. Stream the AI why-line as it arrives — if it is still streaming when the user decides, the decision fires immediately regardless.
known_risks.mitigation: WalkOrderService has a PassthroughWalkOrderService that sorts deterministically and returns static why-lines. The UI never gates on the AI response; the why-line region renders with a placeholder until the stream completes.

known_risks.risk: BriefService cache-per-day contract: the brief must be cached under brief:cache:{date} and NOT re-streamed on every mount. Re-streaming on mount burns AI tokens and causes the card to flicker blank → text on every navigation. Cache is invalidated only on explicit refresh or when the source data count changes.
known_risks.mitigation: DailyBriefCard reads the cache on mount; if the cached date matches today and the source counts match, render from cache. Only call generate() on first load (no cache), explicit refresh button press, or detected count change. KR-099: never flushSync to show loading state — keep isStreaming as local state.

known_risks.risk: OneOnOneSummaryService already exists (backward-looking, generates a summary from past entries). OneOnOnePrepService is forward-looking (assembles what to discuss next). They are distinct services with different prompts — do not merge them. Using the summary service for prep produces retrospective content when the user wants prospective preparation.

known_risks.risk: Async useCallback calling setState after await has a theoretical unmount race. React 18 drops it silently but it is still a logic bug. Guard with isMounted ref when async duration is significant.
known_risks.mitigation: Add isMounted guard (ref set false in useEffect cleanup) before any setState call after an await with non-trivial duration.

known_risks.risk: hydrateSession silently drops items whose IDs are no longer in fresh collection. If ALL saved items vanish, hydrateSession returns null and resume offer disappears with no feedback.

known_risks.risk: tiptap v3 changed editor.commands.setContent to emit an update by default (emitUpdate:true, was false in v2). A value-sync effect that calls setContent(value) to mirror an external/controlled value will therefore fire onUpdate -> onChange; consumers that write that back into value re-run the effect, and if the markdown round-trip is not byte-identical the loop never converges -> the editor redraws constantly (blinking). Also: StarterKit v3 bundles Link, so adding a separate Link.configure() registers a duplicate extension (tiptap warns).
known_risks.mitigation: Always pass { emitUpdate: false } to setContent when syncing an external value (never let programmatic content changes fire onChange). Configure Link through StarterKit.configure({ link: { openOnClick:false } }) instead of adding a second Link extension. After any tiptap major bump, audit all setContent call sites and StarterKit-bundled extensions. See BUG-087.

known_risks.risk: A tiptap FloatingMenu with shouldShow including selection.empty pops the toolbar on a plain caret click and, being appendTo(document.body), can linger after the editor unmounts/scrolls away (BUG-088). known_risks.mitigation: Use the selection-driven BubbleMenu for formatting, never an empty-cursor FloatingMenu. For a compact editor pass maxRows (e.g. notes general: minRows=5, maxRows=10).

known_risks.risk: tiptap useEditor({ content }) applies content only on first mount; it is NOT reactive to a changing content prop. A read-only viewer (MarkdownView) or editor reused across data changes without a key will display stale content when the prop updates (BUG-090: Journal day navigation kept the prior days report body).
known_risks.mitigation: Sync the external value in a useEffect: if editor.storage.markdown.getMarkdown() !== content, call editor.commands.setContent(content, { emitUpdate:false }). emitUpdate:false avoids any onUpdate feedback/blink loop. Same pattern as RichTextEditor/TaskRichInput. Alternatively key the component by the entity id to force remount.

known_risks.risk: KR-006 dates stay local (never toISOString): nextTuesday(fromYMD) returns the Tuesday strictly after the reference Thursday (+7 if the reference is itself a Tuesday); the deferred MEP is nextTuesday(addDays(mesDate, 7)).

App access control is the Cloudflare Access gate on the projetx (app) worker — workers.dev now supports one-click Access. It CANNOT be extended to the projetx-kv (API) worker: the two are sibling *.workers.dev hostnames so the CF_Authorization cookie is not shared, and putting Access on the API worker would 302 every cross-origin SPA fetch to an HTML login page. The API worker stays public, gated by the secret X-Sync-Key + origin-allowlist CORS (ALLOWED_ORIGINS var). CORS is browser-only — it does NOT stop curl/scripts. True API-level auth needs a custom domain (shared-cookie + JWT validation via jose) or a same-origin /api proxy through the Access-gated app worker via a service binding.
